While game availability and bonuses are important, your safety is paramount. Before you select an online casino, consider the factors we used in our ranking process. Below are some crucial safety guides.
Licensing: No matter which platform you choose, make sure it has an appropriate license. Select those licensed by AGCO, Kahnawake Gaming Commission, or Malta Gaming Authority. Platforms regulated by the Gaming Board of Anjouan and the Curaçao Gaming Control Board are other suitable options.
SSL Encryption: The best online casinos in Canada use solid SSL encryption to protect your data and finances. Check the terms and conditions page to ascertain your safety.
Verification: One of the hallmarks of a legitimate Canadian casino. A safe casino will request a copy of your government-issued ID to verify your account. You may also be asked to submit proof of address and source of income. For your own good, choose only platforms that request verification documents.
Game Fairness: Top-rated CA operators use a random number generator to ensure fairness. Top platforms ensure their games are unpredictable and not susceptible to manipulation.

If you're wondering whether online casinos are legal in Canada, the simple answer is yes! However, the legal framework for gambling in Canada is overseen by the provinces. That's why you'll find a range of regulatory bodies across different platforms. For instance, the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario regulates online casinos in Ontario. On the other hand, the British Columbia Lottery Corporation licenses operators in British Columbia.
However, some players use casinos licensed offshore, such as those issued by the Kahnawake Gaming Commission and the Gibraltar Regulatory Authority. While provincial bodies do not regulate offshore casinos, there are no laws that ban them from accepting Canadian players. Therefore, you can register with them, but you may be unable to successfully file for a dispute if any arises.
Please note that most Canadian provinces allow only players aged 19 or older to register with online casinos. Only Quebec, Manitoba, and Alberta allow players aged 18 or older.
Gambling is a pastime meant for fun, not for achieving financial freedom. Therefore, it's crucial to wager responsibly. We encourage you to set deposit limits and use timeouts to control how much time and money you spend at a casino. Use self-exclusion to take a more extended period off gambling if you're already feeling overwhelmed. If you need additional assistance, reach out to ConnexOntario, GameSense and Gamblers Anonymous.
As part of responsible gambling policies, legitimate operators will request your identification documents to verify your account. They do this to keep the platform safe from scammers or fraudsters.
